During hours of peak demand, the Applicant would use the generating capacity of the Bad Creek Project in lieu of expensive, high fuel-rate units, such as combustion turbines.
In the event of system emergencies, the proposed project would provide the Applicant's system with the fastest and most reliable form of emergency generation available. Only conventional hydro is its equal in speed of response and reliability. Should an emergency occur when the proposed Bad Creek Project is operating in the pumping mode, the relief capacity which would be made available quickly would be the sum of the pumping load and the generating capacity of the project. This emergency relief capacity could be twice the capacity of the Bad Creek Project, or about 2,000 MW. Only those forms of peaking capacity which have an energy storage capability have this advantage.
1.2 LOCATION
The proposed project would be located in Oconee County, about 8 miles north northwesterly of Salem and 35 miles west northwesterly of Greenville, South Carolina (Figure 1-1). The existing Jocassee Reservoir of licensed Project No. 2503 would function as the lower reservoir for the Bad Creek Project, and is located on the Keowee, Toxaway, Thompson, Whitewater, and Horsepasture Rivers, tributaries of the Savannah River. The upper reservoir would be located on Bad Creek, a branch of Howard Creek, about 1 mile west of Lake Jocassee and within several thousand feet of the North Carolina State line.
The proposed 525-kV transmission line would extend in a southerly direction from the Bad Creek project substation to the Oconee nuclear plant switching station. It would occupy a new 200-foot right-of-way for about 8.7 miles, and would parallel the existing Jocassee to Oconee 230-kV transmission line for about 9.2 miles. The proposed transmission line would cross South Carolina State Highways 11 and 183 as well as 6 secondary roads and Lake Keowee.
